findings.element: In the 1280 x 900 pair, Future usage now shares a row with date navigation instead of leaving the date navigator on a mostly empty row. Keep mode, lookback and window controls visibly grouped; preserve the date bounds, readable plot labels and all account rows. The capture establishes limited visible coverage, not removal of offscreen accounts.

The screenshots show the labels and visible values, but cannot verify their underlying timestamp sources or establish what lies below the cropped desktop captures.

findings.element: The empty, loading and initial-error pairs retain their clear, distinct presentations: No accounts connected with zero provider counts and Add credentials; Loading pooled quota with Loading on the main action and Awaiting data in the date area; and Could not load quotas with a separate Try again button. Chart-only controls remain visibly dimmed. The footer is more compact in round 4, and empty places its collection/history times into a readable two-column arrangement.

findings.element: All 14 actual round-3/round-4 PNG pairs were inspected side by side, including both upper and lower portions of the full narrow images; the supplied reference PNG was also inspected. Round 4 preserves the dark design, Claude orange, Codex blue, numerical observations visible in each capture, explicit points/points-per-hour units and UTC dates. Provider names, text states, solid/dashed curves and the Scheduled reset legend supplement colour. The shorter headlines remain prominent while their quota/rate labels sit alongside them. findings.fix: Preserve these design and data-meaning cues. This review establishes screenshot-visible presentation only. It does not verify keyboard behavior, focus order or focus visibility during interaction, screen-reader output, actual target dimensions, measured contrast compliance, refresh/retry execution, responsive behavior between captured widths or offscreen content in cropped desktop images.
